To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the class FP(K) of polynomial time computable functions over an arbitrary ring K, is captured by the light affine lambda-calculi typed in the linear logic fragment LAL, and that the BSS model of computation can be embedded in this lambda-calculus.

(a) the light affine lambda-calculi can be used as a framework for the implicit characterization of complexity by LL; (b) the light affine logic LAL, as a logic for the implicit characterization, is more general than the previously known LL-based characterizations, which are all instances of the light affine lambda calculus with a single basic type.
the BSS model of computation is captured by LL.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: given a fixed ring structure, how can we capture the complexity class FP(K) in a typed lambda-calculus?
the question of what can be done in polynomial time in an arbitrary ring K.
a study of computation over rings in the context of Linear Logic.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the BSS model of computation over K is a fragment of the lambda-calculus over K, where the latter is a model of computation in the spirit of LL.

the light affine lambda-calculi are a natural and powerful framework for the study of the computational power of BSS machines over an arbitrary ring K, and that they can be used to characterize the complexity class FP(K) for any such ring K.
LL is the right tool to characterize the computational complexity of the BSS machine.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found a LL characterization of FP(K) in the sense of Terui’s work for P.
the BSS model of computation can be embedded into the LAL calculus, which is a fragment of Linear Logic.
we have given a LL-based proof of the equivalence between the two models.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the LL approach to complexity classes is not limited to the standard ring of integers and that LL provides a natural and uniform framework for implicit characterization of complexity.
the LL approach to complexity can be applied to the BSS model.
the LL characterization of complexity classes can be carried over to BSS computation.
